paragraphs.text: Shaman is a creature type that was introduced in Mirrodin . Appearing mostly on red and green creatures , it was previously designated as the primary red spellcaster before its replacement by Sorcerer in 2026 .

While the word Shaman has shown up in flavor text since the early days (for example Anarchy ), the creature type itself only dates back to Mirrodin (for example Spikeshot Goblin ). That set featured the new species/class model . Creative needed to flesh out the classes and found that wizards showed up in too high a volume. The Shaman creature type was created to help sub-categorize the types of magic users in the game. Afterwards some earlier cards, like Sunastian Falconer from Legends , also gained the type.

Shamans are similar to wizards in that their magic comes from rituals, lore, and years of practice, but their craft has an emotional and spiritual component reminiscent of druids . Wizards were defined as more formally trained, often having attended schools to study and hone their powers. Shamans have a wild connection to their magic; they are common among the more primitive red, green, and black -aligned species, including elves , goblins , and treefolk , whom they serve as protectors and spiritual leaders.

Shamans are one of the five main classes in the class-themed Morningtide , alongside Rogues , Wizards , Warriors , and Soldiers . From the late 2010s to early 2020s, R&D designated it as the primary red spellcaster , one among five classes with special resonance to the theme of Magic . Under this paradigm, the Shaman label was not limited to "primitive" groups, but open to red mages such as red-aligned archaeologists of Lorehold and artists of Prismari in Strixhaven: School of Mages .

Shaman also stood in for the Dungeons & Dragons sorcerer class in D&D: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms . This is because the former fit slightly closer to the Magic definition of "shaman" (as an emotional/channeling spellcaster) rather than the more conventional definition of "shaman" (spirit worker) that D&D uses. Delina , a Sorcerer character in lore, is typed Shaman, and two other Shaman-typed creatures are titled "Sorcerer" in their names. Wild Magic Surge, an iconic Sorcerer ability, is on the Shaman card Chaos Channeler . Finally, Aberrant Mind Sorcerer and Sorcerer Class both being blue while Shaman is not normally a blue class also point to the Red-Blue color combination being represented by Shaman-Sorcerers.

Since 2023, Shaman subtype has been under consideration for a reboot because is has connections to modern-day religions . As of 2025, Design have been choosing to use the type less, because they realized that they had been labeling characters Shaman that didn’t meet the definition of a Shaman. In 2026, Sorcerer was (re)introduced in Lorwyn Eclipsed . It’s not meant as a one-for-one replacement for Shaman, but helps fill in the gap that greatly lowering the usage of Shaman has created.

After this decision, no actual new card has mentioned Shaman (including in Tarkir: Dragonstorm , heavily inspired by real-world shamanistic cultures of Asia), except in Final Fantasy , where Shaman stood in for the summoner job (e.g. Summoner's Grimoire ), which had likely been locked in earlier.
Animists are shamans who can communicate with all parts of land and nature. Nissa Revane was the last animist of Zendikar .

Flamespeakers are a shamanic order dedicated to Purphoros , the god of the forge. They worship strange eidolons said to inhabit the volcanoes and cracks in the great mountains of Akros and are regarded as seers by the population.

Each tribe of the River Heralds is also led by a Shaper, who shares their name with the tribe's river. The magic of these shamans is focused on controlling the wind, water, and jungle environment. They strive to maintain a peaceful coexistence with nature, not to conquer it or defy it. They are called Shapers for the way they alter nature around them. They also summon elementals , living creatures formed from water or tangles of jungle growth.

Temur magic of Tarkir is highly shamanistic, with a strong elemental flavor. Shamans call their magic "whispering" and speak of the frozen memories and even the frozen spirits of the ancestors. During her rule, dragonlord Atarka ate the clan's whisperers, leaving only hunters. After she was overthrown, the whisperers began to return, with the Twice Whisperer serving as the Temur's spiritual leader.

Yamabushi (yah-mah-BOO-shee) is the name given to shamans on Kamigawa . The literal meaning is "One who lies in mountains," which refers to the mountain hermits who practice the ancient shamanic arts.
